-   Potential: narrow candidate taxa, save time, improve relevance
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Research Questions

1.  How accurately can a machine learning model classify animal taxa based on the binary presence of sexually selected traits?
2.  Do evolutionary origin rates of sexual traits provide stronger predictive power than binary trait presence when classifying animal taxa?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data Overview (1)

```{python}
import pandas as pd

#file paths
evolution_path = "/Users/matthewthompson/Documents/Academics/DS Masters Academics/Data Mining and Discovery/Assignments/final-project-thompson/data/animals_rateof_evolution.csv"
family_path    = "/Users/matthewthompson/Documents/Academics/DS Masters Academics/Data Mining and Discovery/Assignments/final-project-thompson/data/family_related_data.csv"

#load data here
evolution_df = pd.read_csv(evolution_path)
family_df    = pd.read_csv(family_path)

#shapes
print("Evolution dataset shape:", evolution_df.shape)
print("Family dataset shape:", family_df.shape)

#info
print("\nEvolution dataset info:")
evolution_df.info()

print("\nFamily dataset info:")
family_df.info()

```

-   **Evolution dataset**: 84 rows, 12 columns; continuous rates of origin for 10 sexual traits (float), with tree replicate ID and phylum labels.
-   **Family dataset**: 1087 rows, 13 columns; binary presence (0/1) of 11 sexual traits, with tree labels and phylum categories.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data Overview (2)

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **SS** — Any sexually selected trait
-   **A** — Auditory trait
-   **G** — Gustatory trait
-   **O** — Olfactory trait
-   **T** — Tactile trait
-   **V** — Visual trait\
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
-   **C** — Male–male competition trait
-   **F** — Female choice trait
-   **K** — Female–female competition trait
-   **M** — Male choice trait
-   **S** — Intersexual conflict trait\
:::
:::::

## EDA — Family

-   very rightly skewed indicating heavy density toward 0 than 1 (binary) and high sparsity in this dataset

```{python}
#| label: fig-dataset1-eda

#family dataset below
df1 = family_df.copy()

# pick likely target + trait columns
all_traits = ['SS','A','G','O','T','V','C','F','K','M','S']
traits_present = [c for c in all_traits if c in df1.columns]
target_col = 'Phylum' if 'Phylum' in df1.columns else None
id_cols = [c for c in ['Tree_Label'] if c in df1.columns]

# numeric & categorical summaries:
numeric_df = df1.select_dtypes(include='number')
cat_df = df1.select_dtypes(include=['object','category'])

# skewness & kurtosis
if not numeric_df.empty:
    with np.errstate(all='ignore'):
        print("\nSkewness:\n", numeric_df.drop(columns=id_cols, errors='ignore').skew(numeric_only=True))
        print("\nKurtosis:\n", numeric_df.drop(columns=id_cols, errors='ignore').kurt(numeric_only=True))
else:
    print("\nNo numeric columns for skew/kurtosis.")

```

### EDA - Family (Plots)

```{python}


#prevalence of binary traits
if traits_present:
    prev = df1[traits_present].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
    plt.figure(figsize=(10,4))
    plt.bar(prev.index, prev.values)
    plt.title("Trait prevalence (proportion present)")
    plt.ylabel("Prevalence")
    plt.xlabel("Traits")
    plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
    plt.show()

#phylum distribution
if target_col:
    counts = df1[target_col].value_counts()
    plt.figure(figsize=(12,4))
    plt.bar(counts.index, counts.values)
    plt.title(f"{target_col} distribution")
    plt.ylabel("Count")
    plt.xlabel("Phylum Name")
    plt.xticks(rotation=90)
    plt.show()

# histograms for numeric (binary will appear as spikes at 0/1)
num_cols_list = list(numeric_df.columns)
if num_cols_list:
    n = len(num_cols_list)
    ncols = min(5, n) #cap grid at 5 columns wide
    nrows = (n + ncols - 1) // ncols  #calculate plot rows so every plot fits neatly (e.g. 11 plots → (11+4)//5 = 3 rows)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols, figsize=(4*ncols, 3*nrows))
    axes = np.array(axes).reshape(-1) if isinstance(axes, np.ndarray) else [axes]
    for i, col in enumerate(num_cols_list): #loop through each numeric column and assign it to a subplot
        ax = axes[i]
        ax.hist(df1[col].dropna(), bins=25, edgecolor="black")
        ax.set_title(col)
        ax.set_xlabel("Binary")
        ax.set_ylabel("Count")   
    for ax in axes[n:]:
        ax.axis('off')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
else:
    print("\nNo numeric columns to plot.")
```
